dictionaryEntries.description: Calvary Bay; 370 yards wide, 820 yards long, sheltered, in southwest part of St. John I s l a n d. 4. B. Long known by the hybrid English-Spanish name, "Great Cruz Bay. " St. John having been settled by the Dutch, the original name doubtless was " Groot-Kruis Ray "; or Danish, '' StoreKrys '' or " Store-Kors " Bay. Oldendorp and Dewitz give it as '' Gross-Cruxbay '' (Ger. ); Oxholm, as " StoreCruytz, " and the Derrotero, 'I Bahia Grande de la Cruz. " Since Crue Bay has come to refer to the post omce on Little Crue Bay, Q. v. , to avoid confusion, the name of the bay has been conformed to that of the post oflice, dropping altogether the name "Great Cruz. " Since this last refers to the " Great Cross of Calvary, " the name I' Calvary Bay " was favored by several well-informed authorities and indorsed by the late President Harding, in compliment to Calvary Baptist Church, of Washington, D. C. , of which he was an honored attendant.

dictionaryEntries.description: Capella Cays; Group of two islands, separated by passage, 60 yards wide, together having a n area of 63. 64 acres, lying 2 miles south of St. Thomas Island. Western of two is named "Buck Island, " q. v. Eastern Island, never distinctively named, is 121 feet high, 320 yar\ds long, area 22 acres; summit in lat. 18" 16' 36"; long. 64" 53' 18". Kid Rock lies ode its western point. Gropp also wanting a name, and there being four Virgin Island cays already named Buck Island, the present distinctive and euphonious name was selected, for several concurrent reasons : Latin equivalent of '' Cabrita, " another name of Buck Island; signifles " chapel " of the Virgins; light on Buck Island, " flashing white ", strikingly like star Capella, called by the Spanish astronomer-King Alfonso el Sabio, " Almenara " (the Lighthouse).

dictionaryEntries.description: Waterlemon Cay; Islet, 30 feet high, area 118 square rods, 260 yards west of Lelnster Point, at east side of Leinster Bay entrance, northern shore of St, John. Described in the Derrotero as, "Cayuelo Acantilado" (steep little Cay), because of its bluff shore, except for a sand spit making out 80 yards sautheost. Overgrown with brush and grass. Named by Oxholm, "Water Limon Kay, " spelled by Knox (p. 223), "Waterlemon"; from a plant there 80 called, the Pae&fiwa taurifoUa, which beam a bright yellow, finely flavored fruit, known as "Bellapple. " Chartmakers converted Waterlemon " into the more familiar " Watermelon " : this last trandated by the Spanish into "Sandfa, " better "Zandla. " Local name, "Jewel Cay. " G. B. , November 7, 1923, restored original name. G. P. "Jewel": lat. 18" 22' 08. 6" (261 m. ), long. 64" 43' 24" (709 m. ).

features.name: Barente Bay
features.description: Barente Bay; Open bight, a few hundred yards wide, midway between Westend Point and David Point, Westend Quarter, St. Thomas. Named on Van Keulen's map (1719), " Willem Barentses Bay "; rendered by Bellin (1764) ''Baye de Guillaume Barents. " William Barens, according to Wester -- 34 of 215 GEOGRAPHIC DICTIONARY OF THE VIROIN ISLANDS 31 gaard, p. 170, was a well-to-do Dutch planter of St. Thomas, who led the reUef party to St. John, during the slave revolt of 1733. Another Willem Barentz was a Dutch navigator, who died in 1597. Local skippers call this '' Pulbedam Bay "; and the Coast Survey field party (1918) renamed It "Regis B a y "; rejected because 5 miles from Regis Point, hence confusing. Geographic Board has approved original name, " Barents Bay. "

" William Barens, according to Wester -- 34 of 215 GEOGRAPHIC DICTIONARY OF THE VIROIN ISLANDS 31 gaard, p. 170, was a well-to-do Dutch planter of St. Thomas, who led the reUef party to St. John, during the slave revolt of 1733. Another Willem Barentz was a Dutch navigator, who died in 1597. Local skippers call this '' Pulbedam Bay "; and the Coast Survey field party (1918) renamed It "Regis B a y "; rejected because 5 miles from Regis Point, hence confusing. Geographic Board has approved original name, " Barents Bay. "

features.name: Flag H i l l
features.description: Flag H i l l; E'OtIli, 980 feet high, 3. !WO yards northeast of Miihlenfels Point, 1, ooO yards east of Havensight Point, on line between New Quarter ilnd French Bng Quarter, S. T. So called by all recent cartographers. Earlier fornis of sanie nnme : Vlnggeberg, Flaggenberg, Flagbierget, Flngberg, Flaghill. features.name: Cabes Point

So called on all chnrts. " Smith Ray Point, " on Holst's manuscript map. Failure of early cartographers to distinguish between Coki Point and Cabes Point caused name Eastend Point to be shifted from present Redhook Point t o Cabes Point. See Amalienborg.

Population (19171, 43, all blacks.

features.name: Bennykenny Hill
features.description: Bennykenny Hill; 708 feet high, on main divide of St. Croix, lh mile south of Prosperity Mill. Spelled '' Benny Kenny "; probably a personal name. Seventeenth-century French plantage " Bequel " was east of this summit. ~ B e d r h o u d tPeak; 860 feet high, chief summlt in Eastend Quarter, St. Uroix. Also called Beverhout Hill, or Mount Beverhoudt. j3ig Isaac B a y; Same as Isaac Bay, as distinguished from Little Isaac Bay, St. Croir.

Also called, Brelds Bay, and Broad Bay. Identical with either I ' Anse de I3abille " or '' Anse de Lestnn " of early French maps.

The plans formulated by Professor Bache, Superintendent of the U. 5. Coast Survey between 1844 and 1866, providing for a systematic investlgation of the Gulf btrepm, recelved a great impetus toward their complete accomplishment, when, in 1884, Superintendent Hilgard assigned Lieutenant Pillsbury to the command of the survey steamer Blake, which, for the ensuing seven years, was engaged 14 the investigation of the Gulf Stream currents from their source In the Caribbean along their course to beyond the Newfoundland Banka By a n original devlce, Pillsbury anchored the Blake in the stream itself, over depths of from % to 2% miles, and secured observations at various depths below the surface, employing ingenious instruments and apparatus of hls own invention. He deflnitely located the a?& of the stream in the Florida Straits and ofp Cape Hatteras, besides ascertaining many important facts pertaining to its origin and causes, temperature and salinity, direction and loclty and position, and the tidal e f f w in it of the sun and moon. features.description: BackefaZl Bay; Deep cove, 400 yards wide between Krabbegan Point and Lucas Point, forming eastern partion of Fortuna Bay, or Fortuna Bay proper, Westend Quarter, south shore, St. Thomas. -Hornbeck, Derivable from either Danish BBeke " (beck, mountaln brook, Dutch Beek ") or ''Bakke '' hill), compounded with I' Falde '' (fall, cascade); hence, Hillbrook-fall "; spelling emendable accordingly. " Northwest of bayhead lies a deep narrow savana with a coconut-grove.

features.name: Barente Bay
features.description: Barente Bay; Open bight, a few hundred yards wide, midway between Westend Point and David Point, Westend Quarter, St. Thomas. Named on Van Keulen's map (1719), " Willem Barentses Bay "; rendered by Bellin (1764) ''Baye de Guillaume Barents. " William Barens, according to Wester -- 34 of 215 GEOGRAPHIC DICTIONARY OF THE VIROIN ISLANDS 31 gaard, p. 170, was a well-to-do Dutch planter of St. Thomas, who led the reUef party to St. John, during the slave revolt of 1733. Another Willem Barentz was a Dutch navigator, who died in 1597. Local skippers call this '' Pulbedam Bay "; and the Coast Survey field party (1918) renamed It "Regis B a y "; rejected because 5 miles from Regis Point, hence confusing. Geographic Board has approved original name, " Barents Bay. "
